classification.difficultyReason: Identify the four exterior semicircular arcs, exclude the internal square sides, and calculate exact and approximate perimeters.

content.prompt: Four semicircles are drawn along the edges of a square with side length $14\text{ cm}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 16, figure to the right of the stem and parts
spec.description: Four outward semicircles on the four sides of a dashed square. The upper square side is labelled 14 cm. No shading. Ordinary source-blue arcs are black under house style; internal diameter guides retain semantic red.
spec.mathematics: Each square side is the diameter of one semicircle. Only the four semicircular arcs form the exterior boundary.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and the 14 cm given remain visible; no answers are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the perimeter of the region, giving your answer in terms of $\pi$.

answer.short:
$28\pi\text{ cm}$

The boundary consists of four semicircular arcs.
answer.worked:
The square sides are internal diameters, so they are not included in the perimeter. Each semicircular arc is half the circumference of a circle of diameter $14\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}P&=4\times\frac{\pi d}{2}\\P&=4\times\frac{\pi\times14}{2}\\P&=28\pi\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
